questions.q: Given $z = 3 - 4i$, compute $z \cdot z^*$ where $z^*$ is the complex conjugate of $z$.
Express $\dfrac{5 + 2i}{2 - i}$ in the form $a + bi$.
questions.answer: Multiply numerator and denominator by $(2 + i)$: $\dfrac{(5 + 2i)(2 + i)}{4 + 1} = \dfrac{10 + 5i + 4i + 2i^2}{5} = \dfrac{8 + 9i}{5} = \frac{8}{5} + \frac{9}{5}i$.

questions.q: Find the two square roots of $-5 + 12i$.
questions.answer: Let $(x + iy)^2 = -5 + 12i \Rightarrow x^2 - y^2 = -5$ and $2xy = 12 \Rightarrow xy = 6$. Also $x^2 + y^2 = \sqrt{25 + 144} = 13$. Adding: $2x^2 = 8 \Rightarrow x = \pm 2$. Then $y = 6/x = \pm 3$. Roots: $\pm(2 + 3i)$.

questions.q: Find the modulus and principal argument of $z = -1 + i\sqrt{3}$.
Given $z_1 = 3(\cos(\pi/4) + i\sin(\pi/4))$ and $z_2 = 2(\cos(\pi/6) + i\sin(\pi/6))$, find $\text{arg}(z_1 z_2)$.
questions.answer: When multiplying complex numbers, arguments add: $\text{arg}(z_1 z_2) = \text{arg}(z_1) + \text{arg}(z_2) = \frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{12}$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Loci in the Argand Plane

questions.q: Describe the locus of points represented by $|z - 3 - 4i| = 5$ in the complex plane.
choices: A circle with center $(3, 4)$ and radius 5
A circle with center $(-3, -4)$ and radius 5
A circle with center $(3, 4)$ and radius 25
questions.answer: $|z - (3 + 4i)| = 5$ represents all points at distance 5 from $3 + 4i$, which is a circle centered at $(3, 4)$ with radius 5.

questions.q: Describe the locus of points satisfying $|z - 2| = |z - 6i|$.
choices: Perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $(2, 0)$ and $(0, 6)$
questions.answer: The equation $|z - z_1| = |z - z_2|$ represents the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining $z_1$ and $z_2$.

questions.q: Describe the geometric locus defined by $\text{arg}(z - 2) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
choices: A half-line starting from $(2, 0)$ making an angle of $\pi/4$ with the positive real axis
A full line through $(2, 0)$ with gradient 1
questions.answer: $\text{arg}(z - z_0) = \alpha$ represents a ray (half-line) emanating from $z_0$ at angle $\alpha$, excluding the endpoint $z_0$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Roots of Polynomials & Conjugate Pairs

questions.q: Given that $z = 1 + 2i$ is a root of $z^3 - 3z^2 + 7z - 5 = 0$, what are the other two roots?
questions.answer: Since coefficients are real, the conjugate $1 - 2i$ must also be a root. Product of roots: $(1 + 2i)(1 - 2i) = 5$. Since constant term is $-5$, the third root is $5/5 = 1$.

questions.q: Find a quadratic equation with real coefficients having root $z = 4 - 3i$.
questions.answer: Roots are $4 \pm 3i$. Sum $= 8$. Product $= 4^2 + 3^2 = 25$. Equation is $z^2 - 8z + 25 = 0$.

questions.q: Find the least value of $|z|$ for points $z$ satisfying $|z - 5 - 12i| \leq 3$.
questions.answer: Center of circle is $5 + 12i$, distance from origin is $\sqrt{25 + 144} = 13$. The minimum distance from origin to circle is $13 - r = 13 - 3 = 10$.
